subject: Request: bespoke uptime appendix + orderform wording for NovaPulse Health
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novapulsehealth.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@novapulsehealth.com>, procurement@novapulsehealth.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: bespoke uptime appendix + orderform wording for NovaPulse Health

Marissa —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to consolidate the change requests so legal can prepare the purchase order. Two asks on our end related to the MSA/SOW attachments and the order form language:

1) We need an explicit uptime exhibit as an addendum to the enterprise MSA. Our target is 99.95% monthly availability for production inference (region: us-west). Please include a latency commitment for p95 inference within 300ms for text-generation calls up to 512 tokens (we can discuss token sizing).

2) Order form language: procurement needs a clear fallback/rollover clause that defines a regional failover path and how credits are applied if we invoke the fallback. Also need definition for maintenance windows, scheduled vs unscheduled, and an exclusion list.

Attached are our current SOW (NP-SOW-v2.docx) and the procurement RFP with wording examples.

Can you: (a) share a draft uptime appendix we can put in the MSA attachments, (b) propose order form text for the fallback/credits model, and (c) confirm what evidence you can provide for monthly uptime (telemetry, incident timeline, SOC2 artifacts)?

We have a target signing window by the end of next week (7/30). If you need a procurement contact call, we can schedule a short 30-min sync.

Thanks —
Laura Chen
Director, Procurement
NovaPulse Health
laura.chen@novapulsehealth.com
+1 415-555-0124

Attachments referenced: NP-SOW-v2.docx, Procurement-RFP.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novapulsehealth.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: bespoke uptime appendix + orderform wording for NovaPulse Health

Laura —

Appreciate the clear ask and the attachments. I’ve looped in Priyom (SE) and Kim (legal) so we can turn around a draft quickly. High-level response and proposed next steps below: 

- Draft: I’ve attached a working draft of a "Uptime Appendix" (RNW-Uptime-Appendix-draft.docx). It includes: 99.95% monthly uptime target, a latency band table for p50/p95, and a credits schedule (tiered).
- Fallback/Order form language: the appendix references an order form clause that defines a primary region (us-west) and an automatic failover to secondary region (us-east) when regional availability drops below the threshold for a sustained period. We propose a 15-minute detection + 10-minute automatic reroute window before credits trigger.
- Evidence: we can provide per-tenant monthly availability telemetry (token-level successful responses vs total requests), incident timelines with root-cause summaries, and SOC 2 Type II report redacted for customer review. The metrics-evidence-checklist in my draft specifies the formats we can export.

Suggested timeline: Kim to review and redline by EOD 7/22; Priyom to confirm the latency table and monitoring windows; Marissa to circulate final redline and proposed orderform language by COB 7/23 so procurement can route to legal and operations. If that timeline works, I’ll prepare a short doc with the order form clause you can paste into your PO.

Open items we’ll flag for legal: maintenance exclusion language, credit cap (max monthly credit: not to exceed 100% of monthly service fees), and whether you want calendar-day or rolling-30-day uptime calculations.

Thanks — will follow up with Kim’s redline.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 650-555-0199

Attachment referenced: RNW-Uptime-Appendix-draft.docx
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@novapulsehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: bespoke uptime appendix + orderform wording for NovaPulse Health

Marissa / Laura —

Thanks — I reviewed Marissa’s draft and attached a redline excerpt plus a short evidence checklist (metrics-evidence-checklist.pdf). Key points and clarifying questions: 

1) Uptime calculation method: we prefer rolling-30-day to align with our monitoring; if NovaPulse requires calendar-month, we can add language but note that rolling windows can be more operationally accurate. Please confirm which you prefer.

2) Scheduled maintenance carveout: proposed to allow two scheduled maintenance windows per quarter (each up to 4 hours) with 72-hour advance notice. Any critical clinical maintenance requirement from NovaPulse that needs shorter notice?

3) Exclusions & force majeure: added standard exclusions (third-party cloud provider outages, customer-config errors, DDoS beyond mitigation capacity). If you want narrower exclusions, we can discuss but may affect credit calculation.

4) Fallback mechanics: draft includes automatic DNS-level failover to secondary region and a clause that allows manual failover for planned operations. Need to confirm whether NovaPulse needs active-active routing (both regions serving simultaneously) or active-passive. Active-active has cost/consumption implications.

5) Credit structure: redline proposes tiered credits (0.25% fee credit per 0.01% below 99.95%, capped at 100% of monthly fees). We can soften the cap or introduce a non-financial remediation path if preferred.

If you can confirm (a) calendar vs rolling 30-day, (b) frequency/notice for scheduled maintenance, and (c) active-active vs active-passive, we’ll finalize the redline and push the order form language (DocuSign-ready) tomorrow.

Marissa / Kim —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the redline. Team confirms the following so you can finalize: 

1) Uptime window: rolling 30-day is acceptable.
2) Scheduled maintenance: two windows per quarter, 72-hour notice is fine.
3) Failover model: we prefer active-passive (primary serves; secondary is warm standby) — acceptable as long as the order form defines automatic reroute and clear detection thresholds.

LGTM on the draft uptime appendix and credit schedule with one small change: can the maximum credit cap be 50% of monthly service fees instead of 100%? Procurement will accept 50% cap. Once you update that, please send the DocuSign-ready order form clause and a final appendix PDF so we can route to legal and sign off by COB 7/30.

If helpful, we can do a 20-min call tomorrow to confirm final wording.

Thanks —
